reflection.text:
Unblinded as nocodazole (CID 4122, name and BBBC021 structure agree) - prediction Microtubule destabilizers p=0.86 was correct, scored as correct by verdict. Review approve was justified.

What got it right:
- Acquisition choice was efficient: starting at dose 6 (1 uM, e2: act_tub_ratio z=+32.3, nuc_solidity z=-30.4) and dose 7 (3 uM, e3: act_tub_ratio z=+43.4, act_mean z=+19.2) revealed the maximal phenotype early with n=188/211 cells. Titrating down to dose 4 (0.1 uM, e4: act_tub_ratio z=+20.1) and dose 2 (0.01 uM, e5: only weak act_mean z=+6.2) established dose-dependence instead of generic toxicity.
- The decisive measurement was tub_mean dose response over 4 wells/doses e10: rho=-1.00 p=0, perfect monotonic loss with dose. Combined with act_mean e11 rho=+0.40 p=0.6 (no clear dose trend), this separated microtubule loss from an actin-first mechanism. This matches e2/e3 where the tubulin component drives the high act_tub_ratio, not pure actin upregulation.
- Reference atlas comparison e6: 10/10 nearest references = Microtubule destabilizers at high dose was the strongest discriminator. This was correctly weighted in hypothesis update e17 and conclusion e18.
- Secondary nuclear phenotype was coherent but not over-interpreted: nuc_solidity strongly negative at all active doses (e2 -30.4, e3 -20.3, e4 -24.2), with frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 e13 and nuc_area rho=+0.60 e16 trending with tubulin loss, consistent with failed mitosis / enlarged/micronucleated nuclei downstream of destabilization.
- Literature check post-unblinding confirmed mechanism: search 'nocodazole microtubule destabilizer' returned PMID 14614453 which explicitly describes nocodazole as a microtubule destabilizer in title, supporting identity; PMID 15389625 also groups nocodazole with microtubule-targeted drugs. No citation needed for phenotype claim itself - search e22 for 'microtubule destabilizer phenotype enlarged nuclei micronucleation MCF-7' returned 0 hits.

What misled / what we missed:
- describe_phenotype e8 at high dose suggested Aurora kinase inhibitors based on visual inspection (density lower, 7 observations, 4 fields). e9 at lower dose suggested Actin disruptors (9 observations, 2 fields). Both are understandable visual mimics: Aurora inhibition and microtubule destabilization both produce large irregular nuclei/low solidity, and high act_tub_ratio can be misread as actin reorganization. We did not follow these, correctly prioritizing quantitative tub_mean dose response e10 and atlas e6 over subjective candidates; hypothesis history shows Aurora 0.06 and Actin 0.04 vs 0.86 for microtubule destabilizers.
- Intermediate dose atlas e7 was mixed: Microtubule destabilizers 4/10, Protein synthesis 3/10, Epithelial 1/10. At 0.01-0.1 uM the signal (e4/e5) is weaker and noisier, so protein synthesis appeared as low-probability alternative (0.02). Budget of only 1 well per dose, 4 wells total (e1), limited power to resolve this - later dose_response p-values e11 p=0.6, e12 p=0.6, e13 p=0.2, e15 p=0.8, e16 p=0.4 are all non-significant except e10 because n=4 points.
- Expected mitotic arrest was not captured: e14 frac_mitotic_like constant across acquired wells, listed as contradicting for Microtubule destabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors in e17. This could reflect timing (cross-sectional fixed assay missing transient prometaphase) or feature definition, not absence of mechanism. We acknowledged it but did not let it override tubulin loss + atlas.
- Cell count e15 rho=-0.20 p=0.8 showed no significant dose trend despite microscopist noting 'density lower vs DMSO' in e8/e9, indicating qualitative density is not a specific discriminator and was correctly downweighted.
- ChEMBL lookup e19/e20 returned 'mechanisms: none curated' - no external annotation to lean on, so call rested entirely on the dose-dependent morphological signature, which proved sufficient.

Why calibration at 0.86 was reasonable: effect sizes are extreme (z>+30 for ratio, z<-20 for solidity) and coherent across doses with perfect tubulin dose response and perfect atlas match at high dose, but still single wells per dose, no replicates, and cross-sectional readout - cannot be >0.95 without live tubulin-GFP + phospho-HH3 kinetics/washout as we proposed in next_experiment.
